consensus_summary: All four blind responses converge on the same core: the Sabbath symbolizes rest — God's creation rest, typologically fulfilled as spiritual rest in Christ and consummated in eschatological rest (Hebrews 3–4 as controlling text). Alternatives listed include covenant-sign, Lord's Day transfer, seventh-day sabbatarianism, millennial-week typology, and liberation/social-justice readings — all of which still take the Sabbath's referent to be the rest-day and its meaning to be rest.
book_summary: The book identifies the Sabbath as 'the complete seven' — the six-and-one unit taken as a single whole at every scale: the week itself, the seventh sabbatical year, and the seven-sevens of jubilee. It claims Scripture calls the week itself 'the sabbath' (e.g., 'seven sabbaths shall be complete,' Greek sabbaton for 'week'), so the rest-day is only the crown of the unit — one-seventh of what the word actually names.
consensus_core_identification: Sabbath = the seventh-day rest, symbolizing divine and salvific rest (creational, Christological, eschatological).
book_core_identification: Sabbath = the complete seven-unit (six-plus-one as a whole, at any scale: week, seven years, jubilee cycle); the rest-day is merely one-seventh of the named referent, its crown, not the referent itself.
boundary_disagreement: The book admits as 'sabbath' whole weeks, sabbatical year cycles, and the forty-nine-year jubilee span — units the consensus does not treat as the referent of the term at all. The consensus's referent (the seventh-day rest) is retained only as a component ('the crown') within the book's larger unit, demoted from the whole to one-seventh.
material_contradiction: The consensus holds that 'Sabbath' names the rest (day) itself, symbolizing rest in God/Christ. The book explicitly denies this identity: 'the rest-day is the crown of the unit, one-seventh of what the word names.' Both cannot be true of the same term in the same sense — either the word names the rest-day or it names the complete seven-unit of which the rest-day is a part. Accepting the book requires replacing the consensus identification of the referent, not merely adjusting its boundary.
rationale: Although the book's extension overlaps and even includes the consensus's cases, its central identification replaces 'rest' with 'the complete seven / six-and-one wholeness' as what the symbol is. No blind response or listed alternative anticipates the claim that 'sabbath' names the entire seven-unit; every alternative (covenant sign, Lord's Day, millennial week, liberation) still treats the rest-day as the referent and rest as the meaning. Because the book explicitly denies the identity of the rest-day with what the word names, this is a replaced referent, not a refinement at the boundary — hence DIVERGENT rather than REFINED, and not NOVEL because it materially contradicts rather than merely falls outside the consensus.
strongest_objection: One could argue REFINED/BOOK_BROADENS: the book keeps the Sabbath category and its rest-day intact (calling it 'the crown') and merely broadens the term to cover the larger septenary structures scripture itself calls 'sabbaths' (Lev 23:15; Lev 25:8; Matt 28:1's sabbaton-as-week). On that reading the book extends rather than replaces the consensus referent. The counter is that the book's explicit claim — the rest-day is only one-seventh of what the word names — denies the consensus's central identification rather than expanding around it. The printed citations genuinely show 'sabbath' used for weeks and year-cycles, but they establish an occasional lexical usage, not that the complete seven is the word's primary or symbolic referent, so support is partial.
